title: Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]
snippet: The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

Senate Democrats demand answers

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”

From the report:

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same issues.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

From The Guardian’s report:

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:

“We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The company added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

	

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps important issues and leaves out key context. The company says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The company defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also says it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out new child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

title: YouTube Music rolling out corner Gemini icon to launch Ask Music
snippet: Besides removing the Samples tab, YouTube Music for Android and iOS is rolling out instant access to Ask Music with a new Gemini icon in the top-right corner. more…
fullText:
Besides removing the Samples tab, YouTube Music for Android and iOS is rolling out instant access to Ask Music with a new Gemini icon in the top-right corner.

The Gemini spark appears on almost every screen in the app, including the Home feed, Library tab, Now Playing, albums, and playlists. It matches Gemini in Gmail and other Workspace apps online, as well as Google Messages in a future update.

Tapping launches Ask Music, which requires a YouTube Premium or Music Premium subscription, as a fullscreen sheet. This chatbot lets you create a mix, discover artists, find podcasts, build a playlist, and ask about your listening history. You can also “customize your queue or dive deeper into artist lore.” In addition to the text field, there’s also voice input.

Ask Music launched in 2024 and was previously accessed from a card in the Home feed.

	

The new access point has been rolling out in recent days as a server-side update, and we’re seeing it on many more devices as of today. YouTube previewed this addition back in September along with “your podcast lineup.” This “personalized AI-audio guide” appears in the Podcasts feed to provide a “quick, weekly spoken preview of recommended shows and digs into why you’ll like them, before jumping into the suggested episodes.”

In his role, McCormack oversaw “close coordination between software engineers and Apple’s camera hardware and chip teams.” He’s credited with last year’s redesigned selfie camera and other projects:

title: Google Is Killing the Nest App. Here’s What Comes Next
snippet: Don’t panic: All your devices should transfer over to Google Home fairly seamlessly.
fullText:
Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices. 

																			Corin Cesaric/CNET
												
			
				

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current users will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant. 

The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.” 

			

More from CNET

What’s changing with Nest moving to Google Home

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google Nest

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app. 

As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch. 

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

Corin Cesaric/CNET

Google says that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app.

Part of the goal is to give users the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser. 

What’s changing with Google Assistant?

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

Tyler Lacoma/CNET

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.

With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

How to make sure you’re ready for Google Home and Gemini for Home voice assistant 

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed. 

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027. 

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

Google

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and users will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information. 

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Josh Edelson/Contributor/Getty Images

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google announced earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now. 

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

snippet: WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

WhatsApp group chats now allows 1,5000 members

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”

Here’s WABetaInfo:

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link.

title: Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday sale brings big savings on under-sink, countertop, and whole-home systems
snippet: Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to tackle some of the bigger upgrades around your...
fullText:
Black Friday is one of the best times of the year to tackle some of the bigger upgrades around your home, and a better water filtration setup can make a pretty noticeable difference in everyday use. If you’ve been thinking about moving to a more capable reverse osmosis system for drinking, cooking, coffee, tea, and more, Waterdrop Filter has a wide range of its under-sink and countertop models discounted as part of its Black Friday and Cyber Monday Deals.

The sale is now live and runs through November 30, with savings of up to 37% on pretty much everything from higher-capacity under-sink systems for larger households to compact countertop models that are easier to work into smaller kitchens or apartments. That gives you a few different options depending on how much filtered water you need, how much space you have, and how involved you want the setup to be. Head below for a closer look at some of the standout Waterdrop deals.

Waterdrop X12 is a smart premium under-sink option for larger households

One of the more notable deals in the sale is on the Waterdrop X12 Reverse Osmosis System, which is now down to $899 shipped from its usual $1,299 price. That’s a solid $400 discount on one of Waterdrop’s premium under-sink models, and you can use promo code 9TO5GBF26 to save an extra 5% off this RO system, which is built with larger households in mind thanks to its high-capacity 1,200 GPD output. It’s a particularly good fit for families that go through plenty of filtered water throughout the day for drinking, cooking, making beverages, and so on.

The X12 uses an 11-stage reverse osmosis filtration system that helps reduce TDS, chlorine, heavy metals, PFOA, PFOS, and other specified contaminants. It also adds minerals such as calcium and magnesium back into the water through alkaline remineralization, delivering a smoother, more balanced taste for everyday use. With that 1,200 GPD capacity, it can keep up with heavier day-to-day use as well as busier holiday hosting without slowing things down.

	

You’re also getting a tankless design with a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio, along with a smart faucet that comes in silver, black, bronze, and gold finishes to better match different kitchen setups. The X12 is certified to NSF/ANSI 42, 58, and 372 standards, and it has picked up some notable recognition too, including being named “Best Smart Reverse Osmosis Water System” by Forbes Vetted in 2026 and appearing in The New York Times Wirecutter’s roundup of the best reverse osmosis systems.

The X12 is easily one of the standout options in Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday lineup, and it’s worth considering if you’re looking for a long-term under sink reverse osmosis upgrade and want strong flow, advanced filtration, and plenty of everyday convenience.

Get the Waterdrop X12 RO System for $899 (Reg. $1,299)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

G6A6 brings under-sink RO to smaller kitchens for under $200

You don’t necessarily need a huge kitchen or a large family to make the jump to a proper RO setup, and that’s where the latest Waterdrop G6A6 Reverse Osmosis System comes in. This compact model is down to $189.99 shipped from its $300 usual price for Black Friday, and you use promo code 9TO5GBF26 to score an extra 5% off, making it one of the more affordable options in Waterdrop Filter’s under-sink lineup this year. It’s designed with smaller households and tighter kitchens in mind, while still offering a 600 GPD capacity that should comfortably handle everyday drinking, cooking, and beverage needs.

The biggest advantage of the G6A6 system is its compact design, which Waterdrop says can save up to 81.8% of under-sink space. That makes it a particularly good fit for apartments, smaller kitchens, or any setup where you don’t want a bulky filtration system taking up most of the cabinet.

Despite the smaller footprint, though, this model can delivers up to 600 gallons per day, which should be more than enough for the everyday drinking, cooking, and beverage needs of a smaller household. Its eight-stage filtration system is also paired with alkaline remineralization to add minerals such as calcium and magnesium back for a better-tasting water.

It’s safe to say the Waterdrop G6A6 is probably the more sensible pick over stepping up to something as powerful as the X12 if you have a smaller family of three or four, or you’re simply working with limited kitchen space.

Get the Waterdrop G6A6 RO system for $189.99 (Reg. $300)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

M6HG gives you filtered hot water without any installation

If you’d rather skip an under-sink installation altogether, the Waterdrop M6HG Mineral Instant Hot Reverse Osmosis System is another solid option in the sale. This newer 2026 countertop model is down to $299 shipped from its usual $429 price right now, and the promo code 9TO5GBF26 gets you an extra 5% off for additional savings. This particular model gives you filtered water plus instant heating in one compact setup without any plumbing required.

That instant-heating setup makes the M6HG a particularly solid pick as we’re heading into the colder months. It can dispense filtered water anywhere from room temperature up to 95°C, or 203°F, in seconds, which means you can jump straight into making coffee, tea, breakfast, or other hot drinks without waiting around for a kettle.

It also uses an eight-stage RO filtration system to help reduce TDS, chlorine, fluoride, PFAS, heavy metals, unpleasant odors, and other specified substances. Waterdrop then adds minerals such as calcium and magnesium back into the water through remineralization, similar to the X12 and G6A6 models highlighted above.

The Waterdrop M6HG also comes with a detachable 1.2-liter glass pitcher, which makes it a bit easier to carry filtered water over to the dining table, coffee station, or wherever else you need it. There’s no permanent installation required either, so you can simply place the unit on the counter and get going. That makes it a particularly convenient option for renters, apartments, home offices, RVs, or anyone who wants a countertop reverse osmosis system without having to make any changes to the plumbing.

Get the Waterdrop M6HG Mineral Instant Hot RO System for $299 (Reg. $429)

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

CT01 is the more affordable way to get hot and cold filtered water

The Waterdrop CT01 Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser is another countertop option worth checking out from the sale, especially if you don’t need a full reverse osmosis setup. It’s down to $199.99 shipped for Black Friday with a 20% discount, and the promo code 9TO5GBF26 for an extra 5% off makes it one of the more affordable ways to add filtered hot and cold water to your kitchen or workspace.

The CT01 can dispense water anywhere from 59°F to 203°F, covering everything from a cold glass of water to oatmeal, coffee, tea, and other hot drinks without the need for a separate kettle. It’s geared more toward everyday convenience than advanced RO filtration, so it works particularly well for apartments, offices, students, couples, or anyone who wants a simple all-in-one countertop setup.

It offers a six-stage filtration system to help reduce chlorine, rust, sediment, and other common impurities while retaining beneficial minerals in the water. Its 1.32-gallon capacity also helps cut down on frequent refills throughout the day, and there’s no wastewater or installation to deal with either. That keeps the whole setup fairly simple if you just want filtered hot and cold water without adding a more involved system to your kitchen.

Get the Waterdrop CT01 Instant Hot & Cold Water Filter Dispenser for $199.99

Use promo code 9TO5GBF26 for extra 5% off

WHF3E-SKH takes filtration beyond the kitchen

Waterdrop Filter’s Black Friday lineup also includes a deal on its WHF3E-SKH Whole-House Water Filtration System, which is down to $369.99 shipped from its usual $530 price. Be sure to enter promo code 9TO5GBF26 to score an additional 5% off. This one is built specifically for homes that rely on well water, with filtration happening before the water gets distributed throughout the house. The WHF3E-SKH system uses a nine-layer filtration setup to help reduce scale, chlorine, lead, unpleasant tastes, odors, and other impurities before the water reaches your faucets, showers, appliances, and other fixtures.

It supports flow rates of up to 15 gallons per minute, giving it enough capacity to keep up with busier households running showers, laundry, cooking, and cleaning at the same time. title: Zane Lowe shares Apple Music Radio audience numbers, recalls ‘crickets’ in the early days
snippet: In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple Music Radio top 50 million monthly listeners

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue said Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:

We were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The issue of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift…

title: You can now assign Gemini ‘tasks’ for free in six countries
snippet: Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free users after requiring AI Pro in the past. more…
fullText:
Starting today, the Gemini app’s “tasks” feature, previously known as Spark, is now available for free users after requiring AI Pro in the past.

Google previously referred to this capability as a 24/7 personal agent before integrating directly into the main Gemini app experience in October. Above the prompt box on mobile (or below on the web), you’ll see “Chat” and “Task.” The first option is the existing chatbot, while the latter lets you “hand off even more tasks to Gemini.”

With tasks, Google’s “goal is for Gemini to save you time and money.” Google shared use cases like:

“Last month it saved us real money after we got hit with a surprise $389 electric bill. I gave Gemini permission to access our utility portal with the new Google Password Manager integration and asked for it to analyze our past billing statements in my email. Gemini worked for a few minutes, and then nailed it. The primary culprit was our heat pump, which it turns out was kicking on around 4 p.m., right in the middle of peak pricing. My wife and I never would have caught that digging through the PDFs and emails ourselves.”

“For our upcoming holiday trip back to Oklahoma, I recently asked Gemini to give me the best options for a USB-C charger. Gemini quickly compared chargers thanks to Google’s Shopping Graph, asked me follow-up questions about the wattage and color, and then helped me check out using the new Google Pay integration. The best part: it also found a discount code so I saved an extra $10. Done.”

With today’s announcement, Google is emphasizing that “Gemini is your best choice as a personal assistant because [your emails, calendar, passwords, photos, files, and payment cards] already lives at Google securely, and you don’t have to send it elsewhere.”

	

Behind the scenes, Gemini tasks work in your own “hardware-isolated virtual machine” that’s sandboxed and has protections against prompt injection, while leveraging Google Safe Browsing when browsing the web.

Related: You can now Email and Text (via Google Messages, iMessage) with Gemini 

Other safety features include having you confirm purchases and asking “clarifying questions if an instruction is ambiguous.” 

Powered by the new Hydrogen model, free Gemini tasks are available in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

title: New gradient icons roll out to Google Messages & Contacts
snippet: Google this week completed the rollout of its new gradient icons with updates for Messages and Contacts. more…
fullText:
Google this week completed the rollout of its new gradient icons with updates for Messages and Contacts.

The icon shapes remain the same for all three communication apps, though they are slightly larger and better fill the circular backgrounds. Contacts is still a head and body, while Messages remains overlapping chat bubbles and Phone a handset. This redesign is not particularly disruptive.

A lighter shade of blue is leveraged, while all feature a gradient effect. This results in the logos feeling less heavy and a bit more modern. 

Google describes the new Messages icon as “sharper, crisper, and clearer than ever before.” The SMS/RCS client did not roll out any other changes with the logo redesign this week. The big homepage redesign is still in the beta channel.

	

Google Contacts was the last Android icon to be refreshed, with version 4.92.26.x rolling out on Wednesday evening. The Phone by Google update rolled out on Monday to stable users.

It took two weeks from announcement to full availability across the three apps.

title: Motorola Razr Fold finally gets its Android 17 update – hopefully the next 7 years go faster
snippet: Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major update for the company’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support. more…
fullText:
Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major update for the company’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support.

The Motorola Razr Fold launched with Android 16 back in May 2026, and it remains a really good option for those looking to pick up a book-style foldable in the US. On top of solid specs across the board, it also carries the promise of 7 years of software support, something that few other Moto devices can tout.

But nowhere was it promises that Motorola would speed things up at all. A little over 3 months after Motorola announced the update and several weeks after other Motorola devices were updated to Android 17, the Motorola Razr Fold is finally getting its own Android 17 update. 

Rolling out now, Android 17 for the Razr Fold is a 4.15GB~ update that appears to be available at least somewhat broadly. Reports are popping up on Reddit including one report from the EU (Hungary, specifically), with another user apparently in a Spanish-speaking region also seeing the update. 

	

Motorola’s changelog explains:

Enjoy a fresh, expressive design

Reduce clutter with smarter notifications

Multitask faster and keep more apps accessible at once

Stay extra secure with enhanced protection and controls

We’re still waiting to see if the update is available in the US (there’s a backlog of updates on our unit), but it’s certainly an update to look forward to. Apparently, Motorola finally fixed a weird UI issue that affected the Telegram app, something we ran into when using the device earlier this year. 

It’s great to see the update out, but it’s noteworthy that Motorola is not setting a particularly encouraging precedent here. Razr Fold is one of the company’s first devices to be promised 7 years of OS updates and software support, and its flagship-tier status certainly would have most expecting it to be updated ahead of some of Motorola’s more affordable, lower-tier devices that were updated over a month ago. Whatever the case, hopefully Motorola will speed things up over the next few years, especially with its $1,600 flagship Signature 27 on the horizon with the same software promises.

title: VSCO launches its first native Mac photo editor with RAW support, batch editing, more
snippet: VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
VSCO today released Studio Pro Desktop, its first native photo editor for Mac, bringing many of the company’s familiar editing tools to macOS, alongside new features aimed at photographers working with large numbers of images. Here are the details.

VSCO comes to the Mac

Professional and amateur photographers just got a new alternative for editing and managing their photos on Mac with the release of VSCO Studio Pro, a native macOS app that brings the company’s popular editing tools to the desktop for the first time.

More than that, VSCO Studio Pro integrates with the company’s broader ecosystem of photography tools, allowing users to manage their workflow from importing and editing photos to delivering finished images to clients through VSCO Galleries, without having to manually export and upload them to another app.

It also supports keyboard shortcuts similar to those found in other popular photo editors, making it easier for photographers familiar with those apps to get started.

Here’s Eric Wittman, CEO of VSCO, on today’s launch:

“Photographers deserve tools built around how they actually work. […] 75% of VSCO Pro members have used our presets in the last six months. Now those looks live on the desktop, with one connected workflow from camera to client delivery and nothing getting in the way.

The first thing users will notice, and then continue to notice when using VSCO Studio Pro, is how fast it is. From changing the grid size, to sorting images, to applying presets by rolling the cursor over each of the 200+ presets, pretty much everything about VSCO Studio Pro feels as real-time and instant as it can be when dealing with large numbers of images.

As for importing photos, VSCO Studio Pro supports Apple Photos, local folders, SD cards, and external drives, and offers RAW compatibility with more than 800 cameras from 20 brands. Users can also choose whether to work with files in their original location or copy them elsewhere.

Under the hood, VSCO Studio Pro Desktop combines Apple’s Core Image RAW processing with the company’s own Reflex image processing engine, which handles presets and editing adjustments.

Batch editing in VSCO Studio Pro Desktop can handle anywhere from two to 500 images at once, which is great for quickly applying the same preset or film-inspired look (including Kodak Portra, Kodachrome, Fujifilm Velvia, and Kodak Tri-X), or making adjustments to an entire set of photos simultaneously, with changes appearing across all selected images in real time.

And speaking of presets, VSCO Studio Pro packs an exclusive one called IOE1 Pro, developed with photographer Joe Greer. IOE1 Pro, as well as VSCO’s other presets, allow users to adjust the strength, color, tone, and contrast, further helping them fine-tune each look to their liking.

VSCO Studio Pro’s editing tools include the usual suspects photographers might expect from photo editing software, including exposure, contrast, fade, highlights, shadows, whites, blacks, skin tone, temperature, tint, hue, saturation, lightness, sharpening, clarity, vignetting, and grain adjustments for strength, size, and color.

VSCO is also working to expand its toolset to include bloom and halation effects, curves, masks, and a remove tool for users looking for more control over their edits and to make more precise, localized adjustments to their images.

Also in the works are new organizational features, including projects for managing groups of photos, as well as culling tools that will allow users to rate images with stars and mark them as accepted or rejected, making it easier to sort through large photo collections.

Once users are happy with their adjustments, they can export their photos individually or in batches, choosing the file name, format, resolution, and compression quality. VSCO Studio Pro also offers resizing presets for web, social media, and client delivery, as well as the option to save the finished images to a folder of their choice.

And speaking of client delivery, users can publish their edited photos directly to VSCO Galleries, allowing them to share full-resolution images without having to export them and upload them separately elsewhere.

title: Honor just supercharged its smartwatch lineup with a new Pro model
snippet: The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks. more…
fullText:
The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the company’s press release:

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

That sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of new sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor says combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”

Pre-sales begin today at €279/£229 for early bird pricing.

Runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

	

During sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor says other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Honor is incorporating a new wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

snippet: Black Friday can turn something as simple as a home water upgrade into a real headache. title: Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
snippet: At the upgraded $83/share IPO price, Anthropic's seven founders each pocketed $280 million, while the company nabbed nearly $105 billion.
fullText:
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.

At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.

Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.

However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”

With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.

$104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.

Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.

Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.

28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.

The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

More than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.

Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet. 

All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

title: The Funniest GTA 6 Memes Are Running Full Throttle
snippet: Online memes and jokes about the game include cats, grocery shopping and Jensen Huang.
fullText:
Even if you haven’t played a video game since Frogger, it’s tough to ignore Thursday’s launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, the most preordered video game of all time. Some companies gave employees a day off to play. (CNET bosses, I’d like the same for the next Animal Crossing game, OK?)

McDonald’s launched a promotion that lets GTA 6 players order burgers and fries via Discord without stopping the game. And CNET’s Andrew Lanxon played it for 24 hours straight at his Edinburgh home, much to his ignored cat’s dismay.

Goodbye to ‘We got X before GTA 6‘

Many of the memes play off a common complaint about how long it took the much-anticipated GTA 6 to arrive: 13 years. 

“We got [fill in the blank] before GTA 6” was the usual caption.

The Marvel Mania account went one step further and listed as many things as possible that “we got” before GTA 6, including COVID-19, a new English king, foldable phones, a second Donald Trump presidency, an American pope, McDonald’s Grimace shake, the Hawk Tuah meme, the Roman Empire trend and many more.

People immediately started looking for a new long-awaited item to fill GTA 6’s place in the meme. George R.R. Martin’s eternal Game of Thrones sequel, yer up!

Now it just goes back to "We got ______ before George RR Martin's THE WINDS OF WINTER"

— Dan Goldwasser (@dgoldwas) November 18, 2026

Let’s be careful out there

GTA 6 might be fun for players, but not for the fictional cops in the game. Minnesota’s South St. Paul Police Department was one of several actual law-enforcement agencies that got in on the release hype, posting: “Our thoughts are with the Vice City Police Department tonight as they prepare for an influx of visitors.”

Touch my cat, and it’s on like John Wick

GTA 6 includes 34 types of cats and dogs you can pet, as well as other animals. If you spend any time on social media, you know cats are a favorite pick. This post jokes about coaxing the little furballs with the “pspsps” sounds.

GTA grocery grab

Sure, you can do wild, crazy things in GTA 6, but you can also… grocery shop? Numerous memes have poked fun at a screenshot noting that Lucia “will appreciate” it if you bring home groceries.

Wrote one Bluesky user, “I think I’m going to spend all my time in GTA6 fixing up the house, buying groceries, raiding gang hideouts, feeding my pet. Total escapism from life where I can barely afford any of that.”

Apparently, you can also pull a Tom Sawyer’s pals and do a little painting.

Check that cholesterol

The American Heart Association got in on the release hype by telling veteran players they’re old.

“If you’ve played GTA on more than one console generation, it’s time to get your cholesterol checked,” one post read. Thanks a lot, Mom.

From Nvidia to Vice City

Some joked that Jensen Huang’s resignation from Nvidia might not have had anything to do with extramarital affairs or backdoor business deals with China. Maybe he just wanted unlimited time to play GTA 6. 

Grand What Auto, now?

Some players complained that you can’t actually commit “grand theft auto” in the game. In reality, you can steal most cars by carjacking drivers or breaking into standard vehicles — only keyless and luxury models require a Key Cloner. Still, the fact that you can’t effortlessly steal every car on sight sparked a wave of memes mocking the game for not living up to its name.

The Burnt Peanut was running into some issues this morning at the beginning of GTA 6 lmao

"wait it's locked?? it's not your car, you need to buy it? sir the name of the game is GRAND THEFT AUTO. i simply grand theft upon an AUTOMOBILE" pic.twitter.com/avSU71JgXP

— The Burnt Peanut Clips (@burntpeanutclip) November 18, 2026

What about us?

And many memes had a sad tinge, focusing on PC gamers who were left out of the GTA 6 launch. There’s still no release date for the game’s PC version.

title: Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio
snippet: After spending months training with firefighters in the field, the app uses Google Gemini to decode distorted radio signals in real time.
fullText:
On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

The Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to update maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” said Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.” 

			

More from CNET

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations. 

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

Improving real-world fire alerts and transcriptions

Reducing the time it takes to understand radio dispatches is only one advantage of the Gemini tool.Watch Duty/CNET

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

The integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets dual iPhone users keep the same phone number across devices

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

	

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

title: Startup sues Apple in India over tap-to-share contacts feature
snippet: A U.S. startup is seeking $162 million in damages and an injunction to impact iPhone and Apple Watch imports to India.
fullText:
Apple is being sued in India by a U.S.-based startup that alleges the iPhone maker’s NameDrop feature, which lets users share contact information by bringing devices close together, infringes its patented technology.

GG Technologies, the startup behind StayTouch, an app that lets users exchange contact details by bringing their phones close together, is seeking ₹15 billion (about $161.86 million) in damages and an injunction against Apple, per court documents reviewed by TechCrunch.

Santa Monica-headquartered GG Technologies filed the lawsuit in India in October after mediation proceedings initiated in April failed in September, the startup told TechCrunch. Pre-institution mediation is generally required before filing commercial lawsuits in India. The company also sued Apple in the U.S. in April over related patent infringement claims.

In its 781-page court filing in the Bombay High Court, GG Technologies alleged that Apple’s NameDrop infringes its Indian patent on technology that helps phones exchange contact details with nearby devices without requiring manual pairing. The company launched StayTouch in 2019, the same year it first sought patent protection for the technology in the U.S. It filed its Indian patent application in 2021 and received the patent in July 2024.

Apple introduced NameDrop as part of iOS 17 in June 2023. The feature debuted on iPhones later that year, with support for compatible Apple Watches arriving in October through watchOS 10.1.

“We are seeking an injunction to restrict the usage of the NameDrop feature which is native to iOS,” GG Technologies told TechCrunch. GG Technologies urged the court in its filing to restrict Apple from selling or importing iPhones and Apple Watches preloaded with NameDrop in India. The case has yet to be listed for a hearing.

In the U.S., the International Trade Commission opened an investigation into Apple’s alleged patent infringement in August, following a complaint from GG Technologies. The startup is seeking an order that could block imports of infringing Apple devices into the country, along with restrictions on their sale.

Founded in 2018 by Gaurav Goel, a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi and a former Goldman Sachs investment banker, GG Technologies developed StayTouch as an alternative to exchanging business cards. The app is available on iOS and Android.

Apple did not respond to a request for comment.

India has become increasingly important to Apple, both as a fast-growing consumer market and a major manufacturing hub outside China. The Cupertino company has expanded its retail presence in the South Asian nation, where iPhones still account for less than 10% of smartphone shipments, giving considerable room for growth.

title: Apple Watch Series 12: Four standout features make me glad I upgraded
snippet: I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did. more…
fullText:
I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

#1: S11 chip makes everything fast

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

#2: New health features and complications

The new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:

Heart Rate

Daily Steps

Readiness

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

#3: Siri Recap

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Here’s what it does per Apple:

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

#4: Faster charging

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:

Apple Watch Series 12: 15 minutes charge gets up to 12 hours battery life

Apple Watch Series 11: 15 minutes charge gets up to 8 hours battery life

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

Apple Watch Series 12 is now only $329 on Amazon, down from $399.

title: Streamline Your Prestige TV Viewing With This New DirecTV Bundle That Has Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV
snippet: This new, discounted add-on will save up to 20% on three great streamers.
fullText:
Loads of limited-time Black Friday-related streaming sales are happening right now, but one new discount that’s here to stay is DIRECTV’s brand-new streaming bundle that rolls Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV all into one plan that can be added to almost any of their subscription packages.

This week, DirecTV rolled out a bundle that combines Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV at a discount while aiming to help streamline billing in one place. Customers with any DirecTV Signature or Genre Pack can add this bundle to their plan, with two notable exceptions: the MyEntertainment genre plan or Premier package are not eligible, as both plans already include HBO Max.

There are two tiers to choose from with the new bundles: a Value plan, which runs $28 per month (in addition to any monthly live TV subscription fees) and carries Netflix Standard with Ads, HBO Max’s ad-based plan and Apple TV, or the Deluxe plan, an ad-free option that costs $43.50 a month and includes Netflix Standard, HBO Max Standard and Apple TV. Either bundle can be added to or canceled from your existing plan at any time.

This deal will save customers up to 20% compared to subscribing to each plan separately. Just note that if you subscribe to any of them, either directly through Netflix, HBO Max or Apple TV, or through another third-party billing provider, you’ll need to cancel those subscriptions before adding a bundle to avoid being billed twice. 

Right now, if you want to watch all the best shows, live sports and news programs, they’re scattered across multiple services, and this bundle offers you three of the most robust services out there, while skirting their latest price increases.

title: Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver
snippet: No space agency has ever staged spacecraft in orbit for a year before sending them on to Mars.
fullText:
NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice. 

			

More from CNET

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water. 

Another 10 months flying through space

The Hohmann Transfer uses gravity and orbits to get spacecraft to Mars without using massive amounts of fuel.NASA

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year. 

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The Mars launch window

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient. 

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons. 

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

title: Instagram finally lets users edit Stories after publishing, but there’s a catch
snippet: Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days. more…
fullText:
Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

No more deleting and reposting Stories

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means users will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:

Today’s update is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting users manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

title: Don’t Miss Out on GTA 6 Launch Week: Here’s How to Take Rockstar’s New Game Anywhere
snippet: Whether you’re on a work trip, vacationing or otherwise indisposed, there are a few good options to scratch your Grand Theft Auto itch on the go.
fullText:
Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may currently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

			

More from CNET

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

Whether you’re taking a flight to the real-life Vice City or you’re elsewhere in the world, there are still ways to play GTA 6.Rockstar Games

PS5 and Xbox Remote Play features will work with a console setup at home

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

The controls for the PlayStation Portal are familiar and easy to grasp for fans of Sony’s home consoles.Scott Stein/CNET

Do some handheld heisting on the PlayStation Portal

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

The PlayStation Portal connects to the PlayStation 5 for remote play the same way as any other device. It’s worth noting that the PlayStation Portal also allows PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers to access a limited library of cloud streaming titles – but this won’t help you with GTA 6. If you want to play Rockstar’s new game away from home, you still need to make sure to leave your console on before you leave the house.

If you’re forced to carry around a whole home console, I’d recommend the PlayStation 5 Slim (pictured right) for its lighter weight and thinner profile.Sean Booker/CNET

If all else fails, you’ll have to lug your console around

GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Yes, you have to have a console for Xbox Cloud Gaming too

Microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

The bad news is that the value proposition of Xbox Cloud Gaming has become notably worse in recent months, as Microsoft did away with unlimited service for Game Pass subscribers. Even if you use this service to play GTA 6 on the go with your older console, you’ll get a maximum of 15 hours of playtime before you have to cough up more cash.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

title: Harbinger is building the unsexy EVs that keep the economy moving
snippet: While legacy automakers tap the brakes on electric vehicles, one startup is hitting the accelerator. Earlier this month, electric truck maker Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D round, capping a banner stretch that includes a $300 million order from FedEx and a new defense contract with the US military. Harbinger is stacking up wins by skipping the consumer EV hype cycle altogether and focusing on the unglamorous workhorses that keep the economy running: Class 4-6 delivery vans and box trucks.
